ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and Regulations, SOR/2002-184 (FINTRAC supervision; reporting of CAD 10,000+ transactions). Provincial (Quebec): Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, arts. 2, 9.1-9.7, 14.1, 28.1 (mandatory ultimate beneficiary (UBO) disclosure for sociétés en commandite); Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236-2262 (limited partnership formation, status and liability); Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11 (French business name and records). Sanctions framework: Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Duly licensed notary public of the origin state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille through the competent authority of the origin state; mandatory for acceptance by REQ and Canadian financial institutions post-11 January 2024

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or equivalent governing body of the foreign general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization as per origin state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization path identical to the constitutive documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against: (i) FINTRAC politically exposed person (PEP) definitions — domestic PEPs, foreign PEPs and heads of international organizations; (ii) Canada's Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (iii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) OFAC SDN List as a supplementary risk filter for USD clearing and correspondent banking. Protocol requires pre-engagement UBO and general partner identity verification (certified documents), beneficial ownership reconciliation under the 25% threshold, negative news and adverse-media checks, ongoing transaction monitoring with enhanced due diligence for wire transfers above CAD 10,000, senior-management approval for any PEP or sanctions-adjacent match, and annual re-screening at each anniversary of the AML file.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.additional_aml_note: The proposed commercial model (cross-border battery-metals arbitrage, lithium carbonate trading, SWIFT LC and wire payment rails) is classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced; no statutory license is required under ISIC 4662 / NAICS 423510, but the LP will operate as a non-MSB importer/trader and must maintain a FINTRAC-style due diligence file for its banking counterparties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Registre des entreprises; online filing via the 'Espace entreprises' portal at www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; name reservation form: 'Demande de réservation de nom'
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, arts. 25-36: the legal name of a Quebec enterprise must be in French. Non-French words are admitted only where they constitute a registered trademark, an internationally known mark, or a historical/corporate name, and must be accompanied by an adequate French generic term (e.g., 'Commandite ... s.e.n.c.' or '... (Québec)'). Non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, etc.) are not registered by REQ; the foreign name must be transliterated into Latin script and combined with a French descriptive token. An English-only name is rejected unless an approved mark exception applies.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank, fiducie / Trust, assurance / Insurance, prêteur / Lender, courtier / Broker, valeurs mobilières / Securities — prior written authorization of the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) required
Université / University, collège / College, école / School, académie / Academy — prior approval of the Quebec Ministry of Higher Education and other competent ministers required

Intelligence, espionnage, sécurité (intelligence connotation), armée, marine, gendarmerie, police, coroner — terms implying public order, military, intelligence or emergency services, contrary to public order (art. 16, Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises)
Royal, reine, impérial, municipalité, Canada, Québec, fédéral — words suggesting government, royal or municipal affiliation and requiring prior ministerial consent
Obscene, scandalous, false, misleading or deceptively descriptive terms (Civil Code of Québec, art. 9; art. 16 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises)
Any name that is identical or confusingly similar to an existing reserved or registered name at REQ (distinctiveness doctrine, art. 15 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A REQ name reservation is valid for 90 days (art. 7, Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises). No statutory extension mechanism exists; upon lapse, the name returns to the public pool and distinctiveness is re-tested on any new application. Practical SOP: (i) file the LP initial registration (déclaration d'immatriculation) within the 90-day reservation window to convert the reservation into a protected registered name; (ii) if REQ issues a refusal, file a written request for administrative review with the Registraire within 30 days of the notice (art. 95); (iii) appeal an adverse review to the Tribunal administratif du Québec (TAQ) within 60 days (art. 96); (iv) concurrently reserve one or two fallback names within 2 business days to preserve the incorporation timetable, since TAQ appeals take 90-180 days to resolve.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. REQ requires every registered enterprise to declare a principal establishment in Quebec with a physical, staffed address at which service of legal process may be effected and corporate records can be inspected (arts. 2 and 14, Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises). A purely virtual or P.O. Box address is not acceptable. For this battery-metals arbitrage LP (no Quebec warehousing or inventory), a serviced-office provider in Montréal or Québec City supplying a physical office, mail reception, record custody and process service is the market-standard solution. The service contract should expressly permit REQ access and document retention, and the address must not appear on REQ's mass-registered-address watchlist.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 15% aggregate probability of an unannounced REQ address-verification visit or documentary demand within the first 36 months of operation at a compliant serviced-office address; probability rises to 30-35% if the registered address is a low-cost virtual mailbox or if the foreign general partner is a non-resident shell company without a demonstrable Quebec nexus. REQ may demand proof of right of occupancy (lease or service agreement) and disclosure of the persons physically present at the establishment within 15 days of a request.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec (CQLR c. CCQ-1991), arts. 2236–2266 (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), ss. 4–34 and ss. 97–100
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; contributions are governed by the limited partnership agreement. Escrow accounts are not required by Quebec law for limited partnerships.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the General Partner hereby subscribes to the limited partnership interest and approves the contribution and capital structure as set out in the partnership agreement; that the registered office of the Limited Partnership be established at [address] in Quebec, and [Name] be appointed as manager authorized to file all statutory declarations; that the manager is authorized to execute all documents, open bank accounts, and arrange for registration under the GST/QST regime; and that the manager is directed to effect all filings with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and to engage legal counsel for corporate governance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online Name Reservation Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a proposed legal name for the limited partnership through the REQ online portal or by paper application. Verify against the REQ enterprise register and obtain a reservation certificate. Ensure the name complies with Quebec linguistic requirements and includes reference to limited partnership status.
required_dossiers: Scanned authorization from proposed general partner
Proof of identity for signing partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a new request with a distinct corporate designator or submit a written explanation and supporting trademark/legal opinion to REQ for reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the internal limited partnership agreement in French (or bilingual) specifying capital contributions, profit/loss sharing, general partner authority, limitations on limited partners, withdrawal, and dissolution. Execute the agreement by all partners. No filing is required for the internal agreement, but it must be retained for tax registration.
required_dossiers: Certified identification documents of general and limited partners
Capital contribution records or subscription schedules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where partners dispute terms, amend the agreement by unanimous written consent and re-execute; legal counsel can arbitrate or certify the amended version.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Declaration of Registration with REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Centre des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Declaration of Registration online through the REQ portal or at a Centre des entreprises service point. Include the reserved name, registered office address, general partner identification, and particulars of the partnership. Pay the applicable filing fee. This creates the limited partnership's legal existence.
required_dossiers: General partner's identification and proof of authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of deficiency, cure inaccuracies within the prescribed delay by submitting an amending declaration; if rejected, refile corrected declaration and pay any required late/amendment fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Revenu Québec Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec – Business Registration and Québécois Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the enterprise number (NEQ), register with Revenu Québec for GST/QST, employer deductions (if employees), and any applicable QPIP. Use the online registration portal. Supply the partnership agreement and NEQ to complete tax account activation.
required_dossiers: Bank account information and director/partner details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax account registration is queried, submit corrected partnership particulars and proof of partner authority; Revenu Québec will reopen the application once the deficiencies are cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Fiscal Bank Account and Confirm Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chartered bank / financial institution and REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the REQ registration attestation, partnership agreement, and partner resolutions to open a partnership bank account for wire and SWIFT/LC transactions. Confirm the registered office and inspect the office lease for compliance and municipal occupancy authorization.
required_dossiers: General partner resolution authorizing bank opening
Office lease and municipal permit if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence, provide a copy of the partnership structure chart, UBO identification, and regulatory AML declarations as requested.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 4662 (wholesale of metals and metal ores) is a commercial trading activity, not a manufacturing operation. Revenu Québec / REQ registration and municipal commercial occupancy suffice.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required for pure cross-border procurement and trading of battery-grade lithium carbonate; only standard enterprise registration and business number are mandatory.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the entity performs no physical processing, discharge, or stationary installation in Quebec; activities are limited to import/export logistics and commercial transactions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to trading office. If warehousing is subsequently established, adherence to Quebec Regulation respecting hazardous materials and Canadian TDGR for lithium carbonate (UN 1450) would apply to storage and transport.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for non-manufacturing LLP. Leased office space must comply with basic fire safety and building occupancy codes from local municipality; no workplace hazardous-material clearance required unless a depot is later added.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST, income tax of certain partnerships, and custom reporting; Revenu Québec for Quebec QST and provincial tax registration. Digital portals: CRA My Business Account and Revenu Québec Cliquer pour affaires.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident Limited Partnership carrying on business in Canada or making taxable supplies in Canada/Quebec must register for GST/HST with the CRA and QST with Revenu Québec. Procedure: (1) obtain a federal Business Number (BN) with CRA via Form RC1 or online registration; (2) open a GST/HST account under the BN using the same BN if not already added; (3) register separately with Revenu Québec for a QST number using the business registration form or online portal; (4) if the LP has no Canadian permanent establishment but is registered for GST/HST as a non-resident supplier, designate a Canadian representative for service of documents. There is no minimum capital or statutory paid-up capital requirement for a Canadian limited partnership, and non-resident ownership is permitted.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: A limited partnership is fiscally transparent; the partnership itself is not subject to income tax, and each partner is allocated a share of the partnership income or loss. Non-resident partners are taxable on their Canadian-source share of income from carrying on business in Canada, subject to applicable treaty and withholding provisions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box entity classification regime. Tax classification follows the legal form under provincial and federal law. Partnerships may make a fiscal-period election under Income Tax Act s. 249.1; a GST/HST substantial-presence election may be available for newly incorporated/registered entities; hybrid mismatch and foreign tax credit limitation elections may apply under ss. 18.4–18.5 and related provisions; QST relief and input tax refund elections may be made with Revenu Québec for selected transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and Quebec QST (Quebec Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 for GST/HST small supplier threshold; CAD 30,000 for QST small supplier threshold. Non-residents and digital-economy suppliers may be required to register regardless of threshold if they make taxable supplies to persons in Quebec or Canada outside treaty-covered exporting activities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently mandate real-time electronic invoicing, fiscal clearance, or digital tax stamping for GST/HST/QST. Registered suppliers may issue electronic invoices provided the relevant documentary and information requirements under the Excise Tax Act and Revenu Québec rules are satisfied. Filing and remittance are generally periodic through CRA and Revenu Québec portals. Quebec is progressively developing mandatory e-invoicing reforms for future implementation, but no operational real-time clearance mandate applies at this stage.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods exported from Canada and to certain supplies of services/intangibles made to non-residents, under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act (GST/HST) and corresponding provisions of the Quebec Taxation Act (QST). To claim 0% for battery-grade lithium carbonate powder, the supplier must establish that the goods were shipped from Canada to a foreign destination as part of the sale, the buyer is a non-resident, and the sale/transfer is not a sham or artificial attempt to obtain input tax credits. Services qualify as exported only where performance occurs primarily outside Canada and the recipient is a non-resident, subject to look-through rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A) or electronic export declaration via the Canadian Export Reporting System
Commercial invoice describing the goods, quantity, unit price, H.S. classification (ISIC 4662), and reference to zero-rated export supply
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill showing Canadian port of loading and foreign destination
Inward remittance certificate or bank wire/SWIFT confirmation evidencing receipt of foreign currency from the non-resident buyer
Purchase order or sales contract setting out incoterms and title transfer (e.g., FOB, FCA, CIF)
Customs broker or carrier records confirming physical export (including PARS/ACI export transmission or cargo control documents)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may deny the zero-rating if the required export evidence is missing or inconsistent. Consequences include reassessment of GST/HST and QST at the applicable rates, interest from the time of the original return, and penalty under Excise Tax Act s. 280 (6% of tax or refund amount) or s. 285 (20% for repeated failures), plus false-statement penalties under s. 285.1 and s. 285.2 for gross negligence. Criminal prosecution for wilful tax evasion under s. 327.1 may result in fines and/or imprisonment. Retrospective clawbacks of input tax credits or GST/QST refunds can extend beyond the normal assessment period where misrepresentation or fraud is established, with no limitation period in the case of fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary authority; foreign exchange and cross-border money-services compliance administered by FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) and by Global Affairs Canada for economic sanctions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility under IMF Article VIII and OECD codes. CAD floats freely with no restriction on inward/outward remittances, profit repatriation, or foreign-currency accounts. Regulatory friction arises solely from documentary and sanctions-compliance requirements: FINTRAC reporting, CRA Section 233.3 foreign-asset disclosure (Form T1135) for specified foreign property above CAD 100,000, and anti-money-laundering KYC for each wire. Partnership allocations to non-resident partners may be subject to Part XIII withholding tax unless treaty-reduced.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds in Canada; exporters may retain foreign currency indefinitely. For trade-reporting purposes, export entries are filed with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) under the Customs Act; proceeds held outside Canada must be reported on CRA Form T1135 if aggregate specified foreign property exceeds CAD 100,000; no exchange-control quotas or repatriation deadlines apply.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility as a supplementary payment-rail accelerator, but legally restricted from true treasury custody. A foreign digital EMI cannot operate a deposit-taking business in Canada unless authorized under the Bank Act or Quebec's deposit-institution rules; at most it may register with FINTRAC as a money-services business (MSB) for localized conversion/payment services. For LC issuance, escrow of capital, or commodity trade settlement, an OSFI-regulated Schedule I bank is mandatory. EMIs can usefully handle intra-group liquidity for minor euro/dollar expenses but cannot provide the banking-grade trade finance instruments required for lithium-carbonate import settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not universally mandated by federal statute, but in practice Canadian Schedule I banks will, for a non-resident-controlled limited partnership, require at least one principal (general partner or authorized signatory) to complete an identity-verification interview in person or via a bank-accepted video-conference KYC allowing remote onboarding if documents are notarized in the foreign jurisdiction and legalized/apostilled where applicable. Quebec's Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises requires prior registration of the société en commandite (LP) with the Registraire des entreprises and current declaration of the general partner; banks will block opening until that extract is produced. Remote opening may be granted only when beneficial ownership is transparent and the foreign jurisdiction is FATF-compliant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered partnership with undisclosed non-resident limited partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart, limited partnership agreement, source-of-funds statement, ultimate beneficial owner declaration for every LP holding more than 25% interest, notarized or apostilled passports/corporate registry extracts, and the current extract from Quebec's Registraire des entreprises showing the general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commodity-trade mismatch: wire purpose codes inconsistent with lithium-carbonate invoices
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial contract/purchase order specifying battery-grade lithium carbonate (minimum 99.5% Li2CO3), certificate of analysis (COA), Incoterms (CIF/FCA), bill of lading, and downstream buyer end-use certificate; every payment must reference the unique invoice number and shipment quantity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border flows from/to sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions, including ambiguous supplier transit routes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Global Affairs Canada sanctions screening, beneficial-owner and vessel/port sanctions checks, supply-chain due diligence reports including Responsible Minerals Assurance Process (RMAP) or audited supplier declarations, and funds-flow tracing to ensure no sanctioned bank or intermediary is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained high-volume purchase prepayments inconsistent with disclosed capital position
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call notices, GP resolutions, audited capital injection records, financing agreement aligning the prepayment amount with underlying trade data, trade finance/LC collateral documents, and written consent from LP partners confirming no prohibited lending or deposit-taking.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For injection of partnership capital from non-resident sponsors, route via SWIFT MT103 to the LP's BMO/RBC operational account; specify ISO 20022 purpose code TRAE (Commercial Payment) or GFIN (Investment/Equity), include the partnership's full legal name, CA-QC registration number, and a board/GP resolution authorizing the capital call. Final beneficiary must match the registered LP name; bank will verify against closed-loop beneficiary list. Because Canada has no exchange-control approval, settlement is automatic once AML/sanctions screening passes. If the contribution exceeds CAD 10,000, FINTRAC large-cash transaction report or electronic funds transfer report may be required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to offshore lithium-carbonate suppliers should be executed via (i) SWIFT MT103 clean payment for small top-ups; and (ii) for major consignments, an irrevocable documentary letter of credit (UCP600) opened by the LP's relationship bank and advised/confirmed by the supplier's bank, covering the commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, certificate of origin, and certificate of analysis. Where supply is recurrent, use a master LC with revolving tenor and quality penalty clause; payments are released against compliant documents. Ensure ISO 20022 remittance advice includes the actual underlying contract and payment terms (e.g., 30% advance acceptable if covered by a bank guarantee).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Delivery FX forwards via Canadian bank under ISDA 2002 / 1998 FX Definitions, with CSA as required
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for offshore CNY or other blocked currencies through licensed Canadian dealers
Cross-currency swaps to hedge long-term purchase contracts and foreign-currency debt service
Vanilla FX options (puts/calls) for downside protection on supplier invoicing currency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the limited partnership's registration in the Quebec enterprise register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of up to CAD 60 (approx. USD 45) per the REQ fee schedule; continued failure after formal notice triggers provisional cancellation (radiation provisoire) followed by permanent strike-off of the registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and related partner slips (T5013 Summary and T5013 Statement of Partnership Income for each partner)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, no later than March 31 of the following calendar year; for a non-calendar fiscal year-end, within five months after the fiscal period closes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty under Income Tax Act subsection 162(7.1) starting at CAD 100 per partner plus additional late-filing charges up to CAD 2,500 for larger partnerships; false statements or wilful omissions may lead to prosecution and further administrative penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Relevé de renseignements concernant une société de personnes (RL-15) and supporting schedule to the income-tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, no later than March 31 of the following calendar year; for other fiscal periods, within five months after fiscal year-end, consistent with the federal T5013 timeline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under the Taxation Act (Quebec), commencing at CAD 500 for partnerships with 10 or fewer partners and increasing with the number of partners; persistent non-filing triggers provincial enforcement measures and may jeopardize the LP's registration status

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is imposed on a limited partnership under the Civil Code of Quebec or the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. A mandatory audit applies only if the LP is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities legislation, if expressly required by the partnership agreement, or if required by a lending or investment covenant.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) at the election of the general partner; IFRS is mandatory if the LP is publicly accountable or constitutes a reporting issuer; otherwise ASPE is the default Canadian private-entity framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: As of March 31, 2023, the REQ annual declaration requires each registered enterprise to confirm all 'ultimate beneficiaries' who are natural persons controlling the enterprise directly or indirectly, and to disclose their name, date of birth, domicile, and nature of control. For a Quebec limited partnership, the ultimate beneficiary confirmation captures any individual controlling the general partner, any individual possessing ultimate direction over the LP, and all limited partners who hold a controlling influence; the disclosure is refreshed annually with the declaration filed within 60 days of the registration anniversary.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners and Capital Contributions
Register of General Partners and Vesting of General Partner Powers
Minute Book / Decision Register of the General Partner

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 150–560 USD per annum (CAD 200–750) for a Quebec registered office address, statutory mail forwarding, and notice handling by a licensed corporate service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 6,000–20,000 USD for a full independent audit of the LP's financial statements; 2,500–7,000 USD for an unaudited review engagement where no statutory audit is imposed

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined headline rate (15% federal Part I general corporate rate + 11.5% Quebec general corporate rate) applied at partner level; the Quebec Limited Partnership itself is fiscally transparent under ITA s.96 and pays 0% entity-level corporate income tax. Non-resident partners are taxable on their allocable share of Canadian-source business income and are subject to a 15% refundable withholding deposit under Income Tax Regulations s.805.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: LP entity-level rate is nil; income is allocated to partners annually. Canadian-resident corporate partners may claim the federal General Rate Reduction and provincial deductions; non-resident partners rely on treaty allocation rules. Quebec incentives that flow through to partners include the Quebec refundable tax credit for manufacturing and the battery-supply-chain investment tax credits under the Quebec Economic Development Plan; the federal SR&ED credit and Quebec research credit are available at partner level where the underlying expenditure is incurred. Net capital losses carry back 3 years and forward indefinitely; non-capital losses carry back 3 years and forward 20 years.
